text:
maria: quick q — I'm updating the postgres deployment in the chart. We want to let consumers either pass values.db.secretName OR let infra inject env via envFrom. Right now my template does `envFrom:\n  - secretRef:\n      name: {{ .Values.db.secretName }}` but when secretName is not set the rendered manifest has an empty `secretRef` block and k8s rejects it. What's the clean helm way to skip the whole `envFrom` when the value is missing or empty?

kevin: easiest is to guard with an `if` around the whole block. helm/go templates treat empty string as falsey, so: `{{- if .Values.db.secretName }}...{{- end }}` will skip it when it's unset/empty.

pat: if you need the block to be legal YAML spacing-wise, do this pattern:```{{- if .Values.db.secretName }}
envFrom:
- secretRef:
    name: {{ .Values.db.secretName | quote }}
{{- end }}``` That way nothing is emitted when there's no secretName. Also `quote` helps if someone accidentally sets weird chars.

maria: ah nice, thanks. I'm actually also using `tpl` earlier to allow consumers to inject small snippets via values (they might pass templated strings). anything to watch out for with `tpl` here?

kevin: `tpl` executes template text from values in the chart context. It's powerful but means user-supplied values can run template code, so be careful if chart is consumed by multiple teams — could be surprising. For this use-case you probably don't need `tpl` on the secretName itself.

alex: fwiw if you want to be extra defensive and ensure we don't try to mount a non-existent secret at deploy-time, you can use `lookup` (helm builtin) to see if the Secret exists in the target namespace and condition on that:```{{- $name := .Values.db.secretName }}{{- if and $name (lookup "v1" "Secret" .Release.Namespace $name) }}envFrom:
- secretRef:
    name: {{ $name | quote }}
{{- end }}``` But note `lookup` requires cluster access at template time (helm install/upgrade) so it breaks offline rendering and some CI checks. Use only if you really want runtime existence check.

pat: also consider documenting fallback behavior in values.yaml: either set `db.secretName: null` vs `""` and call out that empty/omit => no envFrom. People confuse `null` and empty string so a tiny note prevents PR churn.

maria: perfect — I'll update the PR with the `if` guard + quote and add a short note in values.yaml. tagging you @kevin for review once it's up. :thumbsup:
